title: A Surprise Party for Rabbit
summary: The fruits want to hold a surprise party for Rabbit. But they are busy boasting; who will do the work?
moral: Everyone has their own strengths. By working together, great things can happen.
pages: Today is Rabbit's birthday! The fruits in the garden want to hold a surprise party for him. 'We must make a merry party,' said Apple eagerly.
But instead they argued. 'I am the biggest, so I should lead!' said Watermelon. 'I am the sweetest!' argued Strawberry. 'I am the shiniest!' replied Apple. No one wanted to work.
A wise bird perched on a tree smiled to see them. 'Dear fruits, each of you has a strength. If you combine them, this party will be beautiful. Try sharing the tasks!' They fell silent and thought.

'I am big and strong, let me be the stage,' said Watermelon. 'I am good at singing!' said Orange. 'I am great at dancing!' said Banana. 'I am small, so I can put up decorations high up,' said Grape. Everyone agreed, laughing.
They worked joyfully. Strawberry arranged the cakes on the table, Apple hung the flags, and everyone helped one another. In no time the garden became a merry party place.

Rabbit came home and was surprised to see the decorated garden. 'Happy birthday, Rabbit!' all the fruits cried together. Rabbit was touched and hopped about happily. 'This is the best party I have ever had!'
That day all the fruits learned that there is no need to boast. Each fruit has a role, and the best party is born from teamwork. Rabbit thanked his friends. The end.
